name.text: Relations Q3 - How relations and functions connect

questiontext.text: Which statement accurately describes the relationship between relations and functions?

generalfeedback.text:
A relation is any set of ordered pairs connecting elements of one set to another. A function is a special kind of relation with an extra rule, every input must be connected to exactly one output.

Because of this extra rule, every function automatically qualifies as a relation, but not every relation qualifies as a function.

Option A is false because some relations allow one input to have several outputs, which breaks the function rule.

Option C is false because functions can be one-to-one or many-to-one, both are valid function types.

Option D is false because one-to-one relations can also be functions. The correct answer is B.

questionvariables.text: options3: ["A. All relations are functions.","B. All functions are relations.","C. Functions only include one-to-one relations.","D. A relation can only be classified as a function if it is many-to-one."]; tans3: "B. All functions are relations.";
